title: Glacio-eustatic swings of the icehouses, the operator's anchors for the ice slider's glacial-maximum end
note: Peak-to-trough sea-level swing in metres for each icehouse, from the literature. scripts/build_ice.py gives every grid inside an interval a glacial-maximum end: the full swing where the grid sits at an interglacial (the present, whose maximum the atlas draws) and half the swing elsewhere, since the PaleoDEM authors call each grid the average paleogeography of its interval. Grids outside every interval have no maximum end beyond the drawn ice. The ice-free end needs no anchor: it is the stop's whole ice volume melted at 2.5 m per million km3.

intervals.cite: Spratt, R. M. & Lisiecki, L. E. (2016) stack minimum about -130 m; Lambeck, K. et al. (2014) PNAS 111, 15296: 130-134 m at the Last Glacial Maximum. The atlas's LGM map is the drawn target.
